title: Daily scratchpad - GPU ops
content:
2026-03-04 — quick brain dump / todo list for the week

Morning context:
- Spike in GPU memory pressure yesterday around 17:30 UTC on dedicated-pool-3. Likely due to longer seq jobs + suboptimal batching. Need to follow up with model team.
- Host-level OOMs seen on gnode-17 (OOM killer invoked). Suspect driver churn after kernel update?

Top priorities:
- [ ] Triage INFRA-342 (OOM on gnode-17) — collect dmesg + journalctl, get nvml logs, add to ticket. POC: sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 500; sudo dmesg | tail -n 200.
- [ ] Patch autoscaler threshold for gpu-pool-autoscaler from 0.6 -> 0.65 for short term (A/B test on pool-2). Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/456
- [ ] Run rolling restart for driver patch on gnode-15..18 outside business hours (start 2026-03-06 02:00 UTC). Coordinate with SRE on host drain sequence.
- [ ] Add additional alert: "GPU memory pressure sustained 15m" to PagerDuty rule, severity=warning initially. Refer to Confluence: INFRA-GPU-POLICY -> Alerting section.

Quick checks / commands I keep using:
- Check GPU utilization: nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY -i 0 | grep -i "Used"
- Check processes using GPUs: sudo ps aux | grep python | grep -E "--model|--worker"
- Dump container logs: kubectl logs -n infra -l app=gpu-worker -c worker --since=2h | gzip -c > /tmp/gpu-worker-logs.gz
- Node memory/metrics: kubectl top nodes | grep gnode-17

Notes / Findings from yesterday:
- Observed repeated long-tail latency on embedding jobs from customer X. Root cause likely: large payloads + small batch sizes. TODO: ask prod-model-team to flag large inputs at client side.
- One pod in pool-3 had transient GPU driver reset messages in kubelet logs. Possibly correlates with high temperature spikes. Need thermal-sensor check.

Networking / capacity reminders:
- Check bandwidth quota on private-colo-1; we've been close to 85% of egress quota (monthly). Slack thread: #network-ops (see thread id abc-net-2026).
- Add note to capacity plan: if dedicated usage grows 10% mo, need to reserve additional 2x A100 on east-1 by May. Update deck for finance.

Meeting TODOs:
- 2026-03-05 16:00 UTC — sync with model infra on batching improvements. Prep: bring short latency/cost numbers from last 24h.
- 2026-03-06 09:00 UTC — oncall handoff with SRE (remind them about driver patch window).

Loose ideas / low-effort wins:
- Enable per-model short-circuit caching for identical small embedding requests (cache TTL 5m) — could cut a lot of repeat work. Flag for Optimize team.
- Add small "health-check" job that runs a lightweight inference every 5 mins to detect driver resets early. Cheap and gives early warning.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Was kernel update rolled out to gnode-15..18 as part of 2026-02-28 maintenance? (need to confirm with release-engineering)
- Should we throttle long-seq generation jobs at the gateway level to avoid hogging KV cache? (pros/cons)

Attachments / links I referenced:
- Confluence: INFRA-GPU-POLICY (section: driver-rollouts, alerting)
- JIRA: INFRA-342 (OOM on gnode-17)
- GitHub PR: infra/pull/456 (autoscaler tweak)
- Slack thread: #gpu-ops-thread (recent noise 2026-03-03)

Scratch notes (random):
- If I re-run the failing job with --seq_len=1024 might reproduce the OOM. Try on staging first.
- Quick command to drain node gracefully: kubectl drain gnode-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=30m

End of notes.

-- ethan
